title: Kernel sundry docket — Juno Park
content:
Daily scratchpad (short bursts) — aim: keep a compact log + immediate todos. Not meant for final decisions; shove things here then formalize if needed.

03/11 morning: quick triage notes
- Observed P99 spike on canary for small prompt workloads (seq_len ~6).
  - Symptoms: GPU utilization low (~28%) while host CPU goes up and stalls reported from kernel layer.
  - Repro: run microbench 'tinyseq-run' on canary (use bench image bench:tinyseq-2026-03). Step-by-step: 
    1) ssh to canary-3 (eu-west-1-canary-3)
    2) sudo systemctl stop serving-agent && run bench command: ./bench tinyseq --concurrency 4 --seq 6 --iters 200
    3) observe nvlink stats: `nvidia-smi nvlink --query` shows channel errors intermittently.
- Hypothesis A: small-seq path hits a slow kernel fallback (attention tiling) that has a bad host->device synchronization.
- Hypothesis B: NVLINK driver intermittent hiccup on node class n2-standard-gpu-8; fallback path increases CPU waits.

Immediate quick checks (today):
- Re-run bench with env VARS: SERVE_KV_PREFETCH=0, SERVE_BATCH_MIN=1, SERVE_BATCH_MAX=8 (Juno) -> note tls trace.
- On one node flip `LD_PRELOAD=/opt/rdwr_bugfix/libnvworkaround.so` to test driver mitigation (temporary).
- Push a small logging change that timestamps lock acquisition around kv_cache access (PR draft in repo, see linked PR).

Actionable todos (ordering prioritized):
1) (high) Add fine-grained timed logging to kv-cache lock + attention kernel handoff (assign: Juno) — try to keep sampling <10% perf overhead. Deadline: 2026-03-14.
2) (mid) Reproduce nvlink error in lab GPU rack (Diego) — capture ethtool-like dumps + telemetry. Ticket: JIRA-4762. Deadline: 2026-03-16.
3) (mid) Run microbench on dedicated fleet with quantized kernels toggled off to compare (Mina) — collect p50/p95/p99.
4) (low) Document quick mitigation steps for SRE runbook if spike repeats (owner: oncall) — draft short list.

Notes to self:
- If lock timings show long tail >3ms on host side during tiny-seq, look at contention from prefix cache refill threads. Possibly drop prefetch concurrency to 2.
- Check if aio threads are pinning to same cpu as kernel worker threads — review numa_affinity settings for bench VMs.

Weird observation (03/12-night):
- On user-sim with 8 concurrent requests, p99 latency seems to drop if we disable kv cache entirely. Counterintuitive but suggests eviction/locking thrash > compute cost.
- Quick experiment: in local cluster (dev-rack-02) flip FEATURE_KV_OPTIMISTIC=1 and run same bench; results: p99 down ~18% but p95 slightly up. Save logs under /tmp/kv-exp-juno-0312.tar.gz.

Small experiments matrix (plan):
- Matrix axes: seq_len {6,16,64}, concurrency {1,4,8}, kv_prefetch {0,1}, optimistic_eviction {0,1}, quant_kernels {on,off}.
- Primary metric: p99 latency + CPU sys% + NVLINK error counts. Secondary: token/sec.
- Run plan: each cell = 300 iterations; use warmup 50 iters. Automated runner: bench/matrix-runner (PR 9864).

Debug snippets / helpful commands
- Quick perf: `sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 10` then `perf script | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg`
- NVLINK counters: `nvidia-smi nvlink --link-status` and `dmesg | grep -i nvlink`
- Lock debug: add `tracepoint(kv_cache, lock_acquire, %lu, %s)` then `sudo cat /sys/kernel/tracing/trace_pipe`

Open questions (need to decide):
- If optimistic eviction reduces p99 but increases variance, do we expose as opt-in on canary only?
- Is NVLINK error root cause hardware? If so, production mitigation must avoid rolling workloads through that node class.
- Are attention kernel tiling thresholds too aggressive for tiny sequences? Could be better to route seq<=8 to legacy-kernel path (cost tradeoff).

Micro-PRs to land (short list):
- PR 9864: matrix-runner + env presets for tinyseq experiments (Juno) — WIP.
- PR 9878: kv_cache lock time logging (small, Juno) — draft.
- PR 9899: runtime flag to force legacy attention for seq_len <= 8 (proposal, needs perf review).

Meeting notes (sync with SRE / Diego 03/12):
- SRE can quarantine nodes by label `nvlink-faulty` quickly via autoscaler hook. We sketched a simple script to toggle label; Diego will prototype.
- We agreed to test the `LD_PRELOAD` mitigation in lab but not to use in prod without further evidence.

Short-term guide for oncall (copy into runbook):
- If canary p99 > 2.5x baseline and `dmesg` shows nvlink entries: (1) move traffic off node via route:flow=route-no-nvlink, (2) kick autoscaler label `nvlink-faulty`, (3) open ticket JIRA-4762 and add node metadata.

Random brain dump (for future):
- Could try mutex-free read path for kv-cache (RCU-like) to reduce contention at small seq lengths. Harder to land but would be more robust than optimistic eviction toggle.
- Consider adding a small synthetic workload to health-check that exercises tiny-seq path specifically; run at low frequency to catch regressions early.

End-of-day quick checklist (03/13):
- [x] Push logging PR (draft) -> GH link in linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Complete bench matrix run for seq_len 6/16 (queueing now).
- [ ] Sync with Diego and Mina on lab NVLINK repro.
- [ ] Write one-paragraph runbook blurb for oncall.

If I get distracted: drop a one-line summary in #serving-runtime with "pv: tinyseq p99 spike — running matrix, triage in progress" and link to this doc.

---
Small sign-off note: keep this doc ephemeral; once we reach consensus move decisions into confluence/latency-profiles and close related JIRA with clear remediation steps.

-- Juno
